mechanism: Additive anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects
effect: Significantly increased risk of bleeding, including GI and intracranial hemorrhage
management: Avoid combination unless specifically indicated (e.g., mechanical heart valve). If used together, monitor INR closely and watch for signs of bleeding

mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit platelet function and may cause GI erosion; may also displace warfarin from protein binding
effect: Increased risk of GI bleeding and elevated INR
management: Avoid NSAIDs with warfarin. Use acetaminophen for pain. If NSAID essential, add PPI and monitor INR frequently

mechanism: Antiplatelet effect of NSAIDs combined with anticoagulation
management: Avoid combination. Use acetaminophen instead. If unavoidable, add gastroprotection and monitor INR

mechanism: Metronidazole inhibits CYP2C9, reducing warfarin metabolism
effect: Significantly increased INR and bleeding risk
management: Monitor INR within 2-3 days of starting metronidazole. May need to reduce warfarin dose by 25-50%

mechanism: Fluconazole potently inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4
effect: Markedly increased INR and severe bleeding risk
management: Reduce warfarin dose by 25-50% when starting fluconazole. Monitor INR every 2-3 days. Consider alternative antifungal

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2 and may alter gut flora affecting vitamin K production
management: Monitor INR closely when starting or stopping ciprofloxacin. Consider alternative antibiotic

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and CYP3A4, reducing warfarin metabolism. Effect persists weeks after discontinuation
effect: Significantly increased INR (may double) and bleeding risk
management: Reduce warfarin dose by 30-50% when starting amiodarone. Monitor INR weekly for several weeks. Effect may persist 2+ months after stopping amiodarone

mechanism: SSRIs impair platelet aggregation via serotonin depletion; sertraline may also weakly inhibit CYP2C9
effect: Increased bleeding risk, possibly elevated INR
management: Monitor INR when starting/stopping sertraline. Watch for signs of bleeding. Consider gastroprotection

mechanism: Simvastatin may inhibit CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 at higher doses
effect: Mildly increased INR and bleeding risk
management: Monitor INR when starting or adjusting statin dose. Usually manageable with monitoring

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 and may weakly affect CYP2C9
effect: Mildly increased INR in some patients
management: Monitor INR. Consider pantoprazole as alternative (less CYP interaction)

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
effect: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death. FDA boxed warning
management: AVOID concurrent use. If absolutely necessary, use lowest effective doses and shortest duration. Monitor respiratory status closely

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
effect: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death. FDA boxed warning
management: AVOID concurrent use. If absolutely necessary, use lowest effective doses

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
effect: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death. FDA boxed warning
management: AVOID concurrent use

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
effect: Profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, death. FDA boxed warning
management: AVOID concurrent use. If essential, minimize doses and duration

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
management: AVOID concurrent use

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
management: AVOID. FDA boxed warning on opioid-benzodiazepine combinations

mechanism: Additive CNS depression; gabapentinoids potentiate opioid respiratory depression
effect: Increased risk of respiratory depression, sedation, death
management: FDA warning. If combined, use lowest effective doses. Monitor respiratory status

mechanism: Additive CNS depression
management: Avoid if possible. If needed, use lowest doses and monitor

mechanism: Both increase serotonin. Tramadol inhibits serotonin reuptake; SSRIs block serotonin transporter
effect: Serotonin syndrome: agitation, hyperthermia, tachycardia, clonus, diaphoresis, potentially fatal
management: Avoid combination if possible. If used, start low and watch for serotonin syndrome symptoms. Discontinue immediately if suspected

mechanism: Additive serotonergic effects; fluoxetine also inhibits CYP2D6 reducing tramadol to O-desmethyltramadol conversion
effect: Serotonin syndrome risk; reduced analgesic efficacy of tramadol
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative analgesic

mechanism: Both increase serotonin activity (SSRI + 5-HT1 agonist)
management: Use with caution. Monitor for serotonin syndrome symptoms. Consider non-triptan migraine treatment

mechanism: SSRI + MAOI = massive serotonin accumulation
effect: Life-threatening serotonin syndrome: hyperthermia, rigidity, myoclonus, autonomic instability, death
management: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED. 14-day washout between MAOI and SSRI (5 weeks for fluoxetine due to long half-life)

mechanism: Both increase potassium retention
effect: Hyperkalemia risk, potentially fatal cardiac arrhythmias
management: If combination necessary, monitor serum potassium within 1 week and regularly thereafter. Avoid in CKD stage 4-5

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin-mediated renal blood flow; blunt ACE inhibitor antihypertensive and renoprotective effects
effect: Reduced antihypertensive effect, acute kidney injury risk, hyperkalemia
management: Avoid long-term NSAID use with ACE inhibitors. Short-term use with monitoring if essential. Check renal function

mechanism: NSAID reduces renal prostaglandins, blunting ACE inhibitor effects
effect: Reduced BP control, increased risk of AKI and hyperkalemia
management: Avoid combination. Use acetaminophen for pain instead of NSAIDs

mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, decreasing potassium excretion
management: Monitor potassium levels closely. Avoid potassium supplements unless documented hypokalemia

mechanism: Dual RAAS blockade + potassium-sparing effect
management: Monitor potassium frequently. Start spironolactone at low dose. Avoid in severe CKD

mechanism: ARB + potassium-sparing diuretic = dual potassium retention
management: Monitor potassium within 1 week of initiation and regularly thereafter

mechanism: First-dose hypotension; ACE inhibitors potentiate diuretic effect
effect: Excessive hypotension, dizziness, syncope, especially with first dose
management: Start ACE inhibitor at low dose. Consider withholding diuretic for 24-48 hours before first ACE inhibitor dose

mechanism: Contrast-induced nephropathy can impair metformin excretion
management: Hold metformin day of and 48 hours after contrast. Resume after confirming stable renal function

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and renal clearance of digoxin
effect: Digoxin toxicity: nausea, visual disturbances, arrhythmias (potentially fatal)
management: Reduce digoxin dose by 50% when starting amiodarone. Monitor digoxin levels closely

mechanism: Verapamil inhibits P-glycoprotein-mediated digoxin excretion and has additive AV node suppression
effect: Digoxin toxicity and severe bradycardia/AV block
management: Reduce digoxin dose by 25-50%. Monitor heart rate and digoxin levels. Consider alternative calcium channel blocker

mechanism: Furosemide causes hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, which increase digoxin sensitivity
effect: Digoxin toxicity even at therapeutic levels; cardiac arrhythmias
management: Monitor potassium and magnesium levels. Supplement as needed. Consider potassium-sparing approach

mechanism: Gemfibrozil inhibits statin glucuronidation and OATP1B1 transport
effect: Rhabdomyolysis: severe muscle breakdown, kidney failure, potentially fatal
management: AVOID combination. If fibrate needed with statin, use fenofibrate (safer) with lower statin dose

mechanism: Inhibition of statin metabolism and transport
management: Avoid. Use fenofibrate if fibrate needed

mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, markedly increasing statin exposure
management: Avoid combination. Hold statin during short antibiotic courses or use pravastatin/rosuvastatin (not CYP3A4 metabolized)

mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inhibition by clarithromycin
management: Contraindicated. Use azithromycin (no CYP3A4 inhibition) or hold statin

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increasing statin levels
management: Use azithromycin instead or temporarily hold statin

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis
effect: Lithium toxicity: tremor, confusion, ataxia, seizures, renal damage
management: Avoid NSAIDs with lithium. Use acetaminophen for pain. If NSAID essential, monitor lithium levels within 5 days and reduce dose

mechanism: ACE inhibitors reduce renal lithium clearance
management: Monitor lithium levels when starting/adjusting ACE inhibitor. May need lithium dose reduction

mechanism: Thiazides reduce renal lithium clearance via sodium depletion
effect: Lithium toxicity: can increase lithium levels by 25-40%
management: Monitor lithium levels closely. Reduce lithium dose. Consider alternative diuretic

mechanism: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate and may displace it from protein binding
effect: Methotrexate toxicity: pancytopenia, mucositis, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, potentially fatal
management: Avoid NSAIDs with high-dose methotrexate. With low-dose weekly MTX, use NSAIDs cautiously with monitoring

mechanism: Both are folate antagonists; trimethoprim may reduce renal methotrexate clearance
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative antibiotic

mechanism: Both prolong QT interval via different mechanisms
effect: Torsades de pointes, fatal cardiac arrhythmia
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative antibiotic without QT effect. If unavoidable, monitor QTc with ECG

mechanism: Additive QT prolongation
management: Avoid. Use non-fluoroquinolone antibiotic

mechanism: Both prolong QT interval
effect: Increased risk of torsades de pointes
management: Avoid combination. Monitor ECG if absolutely necessary

mechanism: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to active metabolite
effect: Reduced antiplatelet effect, increased cardiovascular event risk
management: Use pantoprazole instead (minimal CYP2C19 interaction). Avoid omeprazole and esomeprazole with clopidogrel

mechanism: CYP2C19 inhibition reducing clopidogrel activation
management: Switch to pantoprazole

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, the primary enzyme metabolizing theophylline
effect: Theophylline toxicity: seizures, tachycardia, nausea, arrhythmias
management: Reduce theophylline dose by 30-50% if ciprofloxacin necessary. Monitor theophylline levels. Use alternative antibiotic if possible

mechanism: Both cause vasodilation via nitric oxide/cGMP pathway
management: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED. Do not use PDE5 inhibitors within 24 hours of nitrate (48 hours for tadalafil)

mechanism: Synergistic vasodilation
management: CONTRAINDICATED

mechanism: Amlodipine inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin exposure
effect: Increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
management: Limit simvastatin to 20mg/day when combined with amlodipine. Consider atorvastatin or rosuvastatin as alternative

mechanism: Both suppress AV node conduction and cardiac contractility
effect: Severe bradycardia, AV block, heart failure, cardiogenic shock
management: AVOID combination, especially IV verapamil with any beta-blocker. If oral combination necessary, monitor closely

mechanism: Additive negative chronotropic and inotropic effects
management: Avoid combination

mechanism: Both suppress AV conduction
management: Use with extreme caution. Monitor heart rate and BP closely

mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, increasing warfarin metabolism
effect: Decreased INR and anticoagulant effect; thrombotic risk
management: Monitor INR frequently when starting/stopping carbamazepine. May need significant warfarin dose increase

mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, reducing statin levels
effect: Reduced statin efficacy; inadequate cholesterol control
management: Use higher statin dose or switch to pravastatin/rosuvastatin (not CYP3A4 dependent)

mechanism: Complex: initially displaces warfarin from protein binding (increased INR), then induces CYP2C9 (decreased INR)
effect: Unpredictable INR changes; both increased and decreased anticoagulation
management: Monitor INR very frequently. Consider alternative antiepileptic

mechanism: Both damage gastric mucosa; corticosteroids impair mucosal healing
effect: Significantly increased risk of GI bleeding and peptic ulceration
management: Avoid combination. If essential, add PPI gastroprotection. Monitor for GI symptoms

mechanism: Additive GI mucosal damage
management: Avoid. Add PPI if combination unavoidable

mechanism: Additive anticoagulant and antiplatelet effects
management: Avoid unless clearly indicated (recent coronary stent + AF). Use shortest possible duration of triple therapy

mechanism: Ibuprofen competes for COX-1 binding site, blocking aspirin's irreversible platelet inhibition
effect: Reduced cardioprotective effect of aspirin; increased GI bleeding
management: Take aspirin 30 min before ibuprofen. Consider alternative analgesic. If anti-inflammatory needed, use diclofenac or naproxen

mechanism: Furosemide may increase metformin plasma levels; dehydration risk worsens lactic acidosis potential
effect: Increased metformin levels and lactic acidosis risk, especially with dehydration
management: Monitor renal function. Ensure adequate hydration. Hold metformin during acute illness with dehydration risk

mechanism: Additive negative chronotropic and hypotensive effects (though dihydropyridine CCBs are safer with beta-blockers than non-dihydropyridines)
effect: Excessive bradycardia and hypotension in some patients
management: Generally safe combination but monitor heart rate and BP, especially in elderly

mechanism: Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2D6, which metabolizes metoprolol
effect: Increased metoprolol levels; excessive bradycardia and hypotension
management: Monitor heart rate and BP. May need to reduce metoprolol dose

mechanism: SSRIs impair platelet aggregation; additive with aspirin antiplatelet effect
management: Monitor for bleeding. Consider PPI gastroprotection

mechanism: Aluminum/magnesium antacids chelate ciprofloxacin, reducing absorption by up to 90%
management: Separate administration by at least 2 hours (cipro first) or 6 hours (antacid first)

mechanism: Calcium binds levothyroxine in GI tract, reducing absorption
management: Separate by at least 4 hours. Take levothyroxine on empty stomach in morning

mechanism: PPIs raise gastric pH, impairing levothyroxine dissolution and absorption
effect: Reduced levothyroxine efficacy; may need higher dose
management: Monitor TSH levels. May need to increase levothyroxine dose by 20-30%

mechanism: Alcohol impairs hepatic gluconeogenesis and may worsen lactic acidosis risk
effect: Hypoglycemia and increased lactic acidosis risk
management: Limit alcohol intake. Avoid binge drinking. Educate patient

mechanism: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9, reducing sulfonylurea metabolism
effect: Severe prolonged hypoglycemia, potentially fatal in elderly
management: Reduce sulfonylurea dose or switch to shorter-acting agent. Monitor blood glucose closely

mechanism: Both increase serum potassium
management: Avoid routine potassium supplementation with spironolactone. Monitor serum potassium

mechanism: Both are ototoxic and nephrotoxic; furosemide increases gentamicin concentration in inner ear
effect: Increased risk of irreversible ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity
management: Avoid combination if possible. Monitor renal function and gentamicin levels. Watch for hearing changes

mechanism: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, blocking azathioprine/6-MP metabolism
management: If combination necessary, reduce azathioprine dose by 67-75%. Monitor CBC frequently

mechanism: Both inhibit serotonin reuptake
effect: Serotonin syndrome risk; also increased seizure risk
management: Avoid combination. Use alternative analgesic

mechanism: Serotonergic effects of both drugs
management: Avoid. Use non-serotonergic analgesic

mechanism: Additive CNS depression; anticholinergic effects compound sedation
effect: Excessive sedation, respiratory depression, confusion, urinary retention
management: Avoid in elderly. High anticholinergic + opioid burden

mechanism: Additive CNS depression and anticholinergic effects
effect: Excessive sedation, confusion, delirium risk in elderly
management: Avoid combination in elderly patients

mechanism: Additive CNS depression, orthostatic hypotension
management: Use lowest effective doses. Monitor for excessive sedation and orthostatic hypotension

mechanism: Dual RAAS blockade (ACE inhibitor + ARB)
effect: Hyperkalemia, hypotension, acute kidney injury. ONTARGET trial showed harm with dual RAAS blockade
management: AVOID combination. Use one or the other, not both

mechanism: Additive hypoglycemic effect
effect: Increased hypoglycemia risk, especially in elderly with irregular meals
management: Monitor blood glucose. Educate on hypoglycemia symptoms. Consider shorter-acting sulfonylurea (glipizide)

mechanism: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein
management: Limit simvastatin to 20mg/day with amiodarone. Consider pravastatin or rosuvastatin

mechanism: Both increase serotonin levels
management: Avoid combination if possible

mechanism: Paroxetine strongly inhibits CYP2D6, blocking conversion of tamoxifen to active metabolite endoxifen
effect: Reduced tamoxifen efficacy; increased breast cancer recurrence risk
management: AVOID paroxetine with tamoxifen. Use citalopram, escitalopram, or venlafaxine instead

mechanism: Amiloride is potassium-sparing; exogenous potassium adds further
management: Avoid routine supplementation. Monitor potassium

mechanism: Diltiazem inhibits CYP3A4
management: Limit simvastatin to 10mg/day. Consider pravastatin or rosuvastatin

mechanism: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP1A2
management: Monitor theophylline levels. Reduce dose or use azithromycin

mechanism: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, markedly increasing tizanidine levels
management: CONTRAINDICATED. Use alternative antibiotic or muscle relaxant

mechanism: CYP3A4 and CYP2C9 inhibition
management: Hold statin during fluconazole course

mechanism: Additive CNS and respiratory depression
management: FDA warning. Use lowest effective doses if combined

mechanism: Additive anticoagulant/antiplatelet effects
management: Avoid unless clearly indicated. Monitor INR

mechanism: Antiplatelet effect + GI erosion risk
management: Avoid. Use acetaminophen. Add PPI if unavoidable

mechanism: NSAID antiplatelet + GI toxicity
management: Avoid combination

mechanism: NSAID blunts ACE inhibitor renal effects
management: Avoid long-term NSAID

mechanism: NSAID + anticoagulant
management: Avoid. Use acetaminophen

mechanism: Celecoxib inhibits CYP2C9; less GI risk than nonselective NSAIDs but still additive
management: Monitor INR closely. Lower bleeding risk than nonselective NSAIDs but still present

mechanism: Additive CNS/respiratory depression
management: AVOID. FDA boxed warning

mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, reducing tramadol levels; both lower seizure threshold
effect: Reduced tramadol efficacy; increased seizure risk
management: Monitor pain control. Consider alternative analgesic. Watch for seizures

mechanism: Thiazide reduces renal lithium clearance
management: Monitor lithium levels. Reduce lithium dose if needed

mechanism: CYP2C19 inhibition reduces clopidogrel activation
management: Use pantoprazole instead

mechanism: NSAID blunts ACE inhibitor
management: Avoid long-term NSAID with ACE inhibitor

mechanism: NSAID + ARB = renal compromise
management: Avoid combination

mechanism: DOAC + antiplatelet = additive bleeding
management: Avoid unless essential (recent stent). Shortest possible dual therapy

mechanism: DOAC + antiplatelet
management: Limit duration. Use with caution

mechanism: Additive bleeding
management: Avoid unless indicated
